metadata.reviewRequired: Deaf-community/FSL-linguist review is required before publishing instructional claims.

lessons.title: Introduction to FSL and Deaf Culture
lessons.description: A draft orientation to Filipino Sign Language as a language and to respectful learning practice.
learningObjectives: Describe why respectful language learning matters.
Distinguish a learning reference from an authoritative community-reviewed sign demonstration.
Identify when to ask a Deaf FSL user or qualified reviewer for guidance.
lessons.explanation: This introductory text is orientation material only. Claims about FSL structure, Deaf culture, and community practice require review before publication.

activities.prompt: A reference is not yet community-reviewed. What should a learner do?
options: Mark it for FSL review and avoid inventing a sign
Replace it with an unrelated ASL sign
activities.correctAnswer: Mark it for FSL review and avoid inventing a sign

quizQuestions.prompt: What is the status of this module's FSL-specific examples?
quizQuestions.feedback: Keep review status visible until qualified reviewers approve the content.

lessons.title: FSL Alphabet and Fingerspelling
lessons.description: Review the alphabet reference and distinguish static letters from motion-dependent J and Z.
learningObjectives: Locate the 24 static letters in the licensed reference chart.
Recognize that J and Z require movement and are not static-frame exercises.
Use fingerspelling as a reviewed practice topic rather than assuming English letter forms transfer automatically.
lessons.explanation: The local Project FingerAlphabet chart is displayed separately under its CC BY-NC-ND terms. The model's static alphabet mode excludes J and Z; this lesson does not claim automatic correctness.

activities.prompt: Order the safe static-letter practice flow.

quizQuestions.prompt: Why are J and Z excluded from the static classifier?
quizQuestions.feedback: Use a future short-sequence model for motion-dependent letters.

lessons.title: Numbers and Counting
lessons.description: Build a review vocabulary for counting and number-related communication.
learningObjectives: Practice number labels with a verified reference when available.
Separate label recall from claiming a handshape is correct.
Use retry and review notes when the demonstration is unavailable.
lessons.explanation: Number signs can vary by language and context. This module provides draft vocabulary slots; sign forms and examples await FSL review.

activities.instruction: Match each written label to its review token.
activities.prompt: Match labels only; do not infer a sign from English grammar.

quizQuestions.prompt: What should happen when a number demonstration is unavailable?
quizQuestions.feedback: Missing media must remain visible as pending review.

lessons.title: Greetings and Introductions
lessons.description: Practice a draft set of greeting and introduction vocabulary with explicit review boundaries.
learningObjectives: Identify the vocabulary labels in a greeting scenario.
Practice respectful turn-taking prompts.
Mark any sign form that lacks a reviewed demonstration.
lessons.explanation: The labels below are content-management entries, not verified FSL definitions. A reviewer must confirm each sign, gloss, and usage context.

activities.prompt: A learner wants to introduce themselves but no validated media is available.
options: Use a placeholder and request review
activities.correctAnswer: Use a placeholder and request review

quizQuestions.prompt: What should be validated before publishing a greeting example?
quizQuestions.feedback: FSL teaching content requires linguistic and community review.

lessons.title: Family and Relationships
lessons.description: Review family vocabulary as labeled practice content while awaiting sign-form validation.
learningObjectives: Recognize family vocabulary labels.
Practice matching a label to a content-management entry.
Avoid treating English kinship structure as an FSL grammar rule.
lessons.explanation: Family terms may have language-specific forms and usage. Examples remain draft material pending review by an FSL linguist and Deaf-community reviewer.

activities.instruction: Match the label to the draft vocabulary ID.
activities.prompt: This checks navigation and vocabulary labels, not sign accuracy.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does a pending review status mean?
quizQuestions.feedback: Do not publish or score unreviewed examples.

lessons.title: Everyday Activities
lessons.description: Organize draft everyday-activity vocabulary for later reviewed practice.
learningObjectives: Recognize everyday vocabulary labels.
Distinguish content organization from a grammar lesson.
Use missing-media states safely.
lessons.explanation: The module intentionally avoids asserting English-like sentence order or sign meanings. FSL examples await source and community validation.

activities.prompt: Prepare a draft activity without inventing media.

quizQuestions.prompt: What is the safe response to a missing sign video?
quizQuestions.feedback: The app must not imply that placeholder media is authentic FSL.

lessons.title: School and Classroom
lessons.description: Prepare school-related vocabulary and classroom practice slots for review.
learningObjectives: Identify school vocabulary labels.
Practice a classroom scenario choice without asserting FSL syntax.
Locate pending source and media status.
lessons.explanation: DepEd identifies FSL as the target language in its K–3 FSL curriculum resource. This module uses that curriculum as a reference pointer, not as republished instructional content.

activities.prompt: A classroom example has no reviewed demonstration. What should the learner see?

quizQuestions.prompt: Which source is a curriculum reference in this draft?
quizQuestions.feedback: Use the source as a research reference and respect its copyright terms.

lessons.title: Common Conversations
lessons.description: Combine draft vocabulary into scenario prompts while clearly separating recognition from language correctness.
learningObjectives: Select vocabulary for a simple scenario.
Distinguish model label agreement from fluent FSL communication.
Review unresolved content before publication.
lessons.explanation: This module is a scenario scaffold only. It does not assert FSL word order, facial grammar, or conversational norms without review.

activities.prompt: A learner needs a hospital scenario, but no validated sign media is attached.
options: Keep the scenario marked pending review
activities.correctAnswer: Keep the scenario marked pending review

quizQuestions.prompt: Does model agreement prove that an authentic FSL sign was performed?
options: No, it is provisional recognition feedback
quizQuestions.correctAnswer: No, it is provisional recognition feedback
quizQuestions.feedback: Recognition output and language validation are separate concerns.

grammarExercises.explanation: This is a structural exercise scaffold, not an asserted FSL word-order rule.

grammarExercises.promptText: Draft review: identify the facial or body cue that requires expert validation.
grammarExercises.explanation: Non-manual signals are language-specific and must not be inferred from spoken-language punctuation.

grammarExercises.promptText: Draft review: arrange the question scenario tokens for FSL linguist validation.
grammarExercises.explanation: Question structure and non-manual marking are pending FSL-specific review.

quizQuestions.prompt: Should English question order be copied directly into FSL?
options: No, verify FSL structure with a qualified source
quizQuestions.correctAnswer: No, verify FSL structure with a qualified source

grammarExercises.promptText: Draft review: order time-reference tokens only after the intended FSL structure is validated.
grammarExercises.explanation: Time reference, aspect, and sequence require FSL-specific linguistic review; no English-to-FSL rule is assumed here.

grammarExercises.promptText: Draft review: match each learning goal to the safe practice action.
grammarExercises.explanation: This activity checks whether learners can separate vocabulary selection from an unverified claim about FSL structure.

quizQuestions.feedback: The activity is a scaffold until a qualified FSL reviewer approves the structure.

grammarExercises.promptText: Draft review: arrange the scenario tokens, then compare the result with reviewed FSL guidance.
grammarExercises.explanation: The order shown is a practice placeholder. It must not be presented as authoritative FSL syntax before review.

quizQuestions.prompt: What should happen before this ordering becomes instructional?
quizQuestions.feedback: Language structure needs linguistic and community validation.

grammarExercises.promptText: Draft review: identify which non-manual cue requires expert confirmation.
grammarExercises.explanation: Facial expression, gaze, posture, and movement can carry language-specific information; this exercise does not define those patterns.

quizQuestions.prompt: How should a learner treat an unreviewed non-manual cue?
quizQuestions.feedback: Do not infer FSL grammar from English punctuation or another signed language.

grammarExercises.promptText: Draft review: choose the safest response when a facial-grammar example is unavailable.
grammarExercises.explanation: The scenario trains review behavior rather than teaching a specific facial or body grammar pattern.

quizQuestions.prompt: What is the safe response to missing non-manual media?
quizQuestions.feedback: The app should make uncertainty visible instead of presenting an invented demonstration.

grammarExercises.promptText: Draft review: match a question scenario to the correct review action.
grammarExercises.explanation: Question meaning and structure are kept separate from English word order until FSL-specific guidance is confirmed.

quizQuestions.feedback: This activity helps organize review without claiming that English and FSL questions have the same structure.

grammarExercises.promptText: Draft review: arrange a question scenario for later FSL linguist validation.
grammarExercises.explanation: The displayed order is a draft scenario only. FSL question structure and non-manual marking remain unresolved.

quizQuestions.prompt: Should English question order be copied directly into FSL?
options: Only when the app is offline
quizQuestions.feedback: A qualified FSL source must validate the structure before publication.

grammarExercises.promptText: Draft review: match a time-reference question to the appropriate review note.
grammarExercises.explanation: Time, aspect, and sequence are language-specific. This activity organizes questions for later review rather than defining them.

quizQuestions.prompt: What should a learner do with an unverified time-reference pattern?
quizQuestions.feedback: Keep unresolved grammar visible until expert validation is complete.

grammarExercises.promptText: Draft review: arrange a daily-life scenario while keeping time-reference claims provisional.
grammarExercises.explanation: This is a draft practice sequence connected to everyday vocabulary; it is not an approved FSL tense or aspect lesson.
